**Presented in class on {{< var project-design-review-dates >}}.**

Your team will sign up for a 10-minute in-class presentation shortly after your proposal debrief. The purpose of the presentation is to share the plan for your project with your classmates and solicit their feedback.

Your presentation should include a 3-minute overview of your project followed by an in-depth presentation of a specific technical problem your team is working on and has not yet solved. The goal is to get useful input from other students, so you must explain the problem clearly enough for them to give meaningful suggestions.

## Requirements

You are free to structure your presentation however you like, but most successful presentations include the following components:

- **Introduction**: introduce the problem statement and the objectives of the project. What are you trying to achieve? What inspired you to choose this project?
- **Specifications**: What will your project do?
- **Implementation**: Present a block diagram of your system.
  - What is the role of the MCU and the FPGA?
  - What new hardware are you using?
  - What new MCU peripheral(s) are you planning to use?
- **Feedback**: Solicit feedback from your peers. This requires some thought and intentionality to do well. The goal is to solicit feedback on a technical topic, not just a high-level implementation detail (e.g., what color to paint the box). Some ideas to consider:
  - What technical problem would you like feedback on from your peers?
  - How would you like them to provide that feedback?
- **Conclusion and Q&A**: Briefly conclude the presentation and field questions from the audience (as time allows).

## Grading Rubric

The design review presentation is worth 20% of your project grade, graded according to the rubric below. Each of the four categories below is worth 5 points.

| Category | 5 pts | 2.5 pts | 0 pts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overview of Project & Status Update | Easy to understand goal of project and project architecture, and currently implemented subsystems are clear. | Goal of project is clear with some representation of architecture. Some understanding of what has been implemented. | Little communication of either goal or architecture of project. Can't tell what is done and what is not. |
| Description of Subsystem | Subsystem described concisely, but in sufficient technical detail to ask questions. | Subsystem described in a confusing way or lacks technical depth. | Cannot understand subsystem. |
| Meaningful Feedback from Audience | Audience asks questions or offers advice that indicates understanding and helps advance the project. | Audience asks clarifying questions and achieves understanding. | Audience asks few questions or does not reach useful conclusions about the project. |
| Presentation | Presentation is practiced and well ordered to facilitate audience understanding. | Presentation has reasonable organization and presenters may be stiff. | Presentation is unrehearsed, organization is weak. |

**Total: 20 points (5 points × 4 categories)**
